messages:
sam: quick Q — who actually owns user-facing traffic-splits: feature flags pushed by apps or rollout policies configured in the console?

nina: console rollout policies. flags are app-owned for local/experiment toggles. but i keep seeing overrides at runtime..?

kevin: problem we hit: SDK-level feature flag (dev toggle) can short-circuit the router and bypass policy guards. not ideal for compliance canaries.

liz: this is the core ambiguity. we have three config surfaces: 1) code-level flags (SDK), 2) rollout policies (console/ctl), 3) runtime API params (route-level). precedence isn't documented.

sam: exact. example we saw:
```
# rollout policy (console)
{ "route": "chat.v1", "split": [{"model":"redwood-1","pct": 5}, {"model":"redwood-2","pct":95}] }
# feature flag in SDK
feature.set('use-redwood-1', true)
```
which one should win?

nina: for safety/compliance we always want console policies to be able to enforce guard rails (canaries, geo, paid-tier). SDK flags should be lower priority unless explicitly granted.

kevin: agreed but current runtime logic is "most-recent-local" wins. that's why a dev toggle accidentally routed 100% to redwood-1 during a canary.

liz: proposal: define an explicit precedence matrix:
- admin rollout policy (console, system) = highest
- runtime API override (service-to-service operator) = middle but auditable
- sdk/local feature flags = lowest by default

sam: +1. also need to expose "origin" in telemetry (route decisions) so ops can trace who/what flipped the split. e.g. origin: console|api-key|sdk.<user>

kevin: telemetry addition would help. add also a short audit event on policy-eval when a flag overrides policy: we should log policy_id and flag_id.

nina: UI change idea: show effective split with pill UI and an explanation line: "effective split: 5% redwood-1 (console canary) — overridden by sdk flag? click to inspect origin"

sam: edge-case: what if console wants to delegate a specific route to a team (allow SDK to control within guard)? might need an opt-in delegate bit on policy:
```
{ "route": "chat.v1", "delegate_sdk": true, "max_pct": 20 }
```
then sdk can only set within 0..max_pct.

liz: liked that. adds expressiveness without losing system-level control. we must enforce at runtime.

deploy-bot: deploy preview: rollout-precedence-doc updated in RFC branch PR #4823 — tests for "delegate_sdk" added.

kevin: next actions: 1) RFC for precedence matrix + delegate bit (I can author) 2) telemetry schema change (origin+audit ids) 3) console UX mock for effective-split inspector. who wants to pair on the RFC?

nina: i can pair on telemetry and UX bits.

sam: i'll help with runtime enforcement tests. add me to the PR.

liz: great. kevin, put a short section in RFC with examples and failure modes. aim to land before next sprint.

sam: thanks — i'll follow up in the RFC thread with concrete API examples and test cases.
